newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht steady late after G7, interbank eases.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht steady late after G7, interbank eases.

text.p: The Thai baht held steady late on Monday after a weekend G7 meeting halted dollar rallies and gave the battered baht some relief, traders said.
Dollar/baht stayed largely steady in a 25.935/25.950 bid/offer range late on Monday against 25.930/25.950 in the morning, traders said.
"It's been steady for most of the day, with the market quiet bacause of the holiday in Singapore and the G7 announcement has affected dollar/yen," said a dealer at Siam Commercial Bank.
G7 ministers said over the weekend they disapproved of irrational movements in foreign exchange markets.

The dollar, easing early against the yen after the meeting, firmed in the afternoon to 122.65/122.70 yen late on Monday from 122.46/122.49 earlier in the morning. It had breached 123 yen mark last week.
The dollar's late gains against the yen may lead the baht weakening against the greenback on Tuesday, traders said.
"That doesn't look so good, though there is some positive news in swaps coming down," she said.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium fell to 16 satangs per dollar from a 19.50-20.50 high early on Monday, dealers said.

The overnight interbank rate eased to 18-20 percent late on Monday from 24-25 in the morning on a gradual return of funds withdrawn earlier for Lunar New Year spending and after commercial bank reserve requirements last week, traders said.
Liquidity was expected to ease further on Tuesday with more funds flowing back into the system, they said.
